public_rationale: Marcus wrote on 15 January 2025 that all we would have that year were agent demos. The window ended on 31 December 2025. Under the contract's plain reading, the sentence covers agent products in general. It does not carry the 'narrow use cases' exception from the sentence before it. Anthropic says Claude Code became generally available in May 2025 and became a critical tool for firms including Netflix, Spotify and KPMG. Anthropic also says it reached $1 billion in run-rate revenue in November 2025. Salesforce reported more than 9,500 paid Agentforce deals as of the quarter ending 31 October 2025, and a 70% quarterly rise in Agentforce accounts in production. These disclosures show paid production use in 2025, which meets the contradiction condition. A benchmark paper from 30 October 2025 found that the best agent automated 2.5% of the real-world projects in its Remote Labor Index. That bears on his point about reliability. It does not show that agent products were only demos.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'demos' as covering all AI agent products, not only general-purpose ones.
Coding agents and customer-service agents might count as the 'narrow use cases' he allowed in the previous sentence.
Run-rate revenue and deal counts are company-reported figures, not audited annual revenue.
The benchmark measures performance on a fixed set of projects, not reliability in deployed products.

criteria.contradiction_condition: During 2025, AI agent products were generally available and in real production use with paying customers at meaningful scale.

evidence.explanation: An agentic coding product was generally available from May 2025 and used by major companies. That is more than a demo.

evidence.explanation: A $1 billion revenue run rate within 2025 shows large-scale paid use of an agent product. This is a run rate, not realized annual revenue. It is cited only as evidence of real use.
